title: Iterables and iterators
learningObjectives: Explain iterables and iterators and use JavaScript collections and iteration safely.

understand.concept: An iterable provides a Symbol.iterator method that returns an iterator. An iterator provides next() and returns {value, done} results. Arrays, strings, Maps, and Sets are built-in iterables. for...of consumes the iterable protocol.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding the protocol explains how for...of, spread syntax, and destructuring consume different collections. Custom iterables can expose data in a controlled sequence.
understand.analogy: An iterable is a collection that knows how to hand out its next item; the iterator is the handout process.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; collection identity, iteration, and binary storage follow JavaScript specification rules.

explain.narrative: Each next call returns a value and a done flag. After the sequence ends, done is true.

examples.explanation: Each next call returns a value and a done flag. After the sequence ends, done is true.
examples.expectedOutput: Console output demonstrates the collection, iteration, or copying behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Inspect the iterator for a string and a Map. Write a small custom iterable that yields three values.
practise.independentTask: Choose an appropriate collection or iteration technique for a small data task. Test duplicates, ordering, identity, and copying behaviour.
hints: Check whether a method mutates its receiver.
Remember that object equality is based on identity.
Use typed arrays only when binary data semantics are needed.
